stat3_label: steps to target at 12 qubits (global), 1024 → 10k shots
q1_answer: Local: 11–29 shots up to 14 qubits; global: ×3.5 per 2 qubits (790 at 12). In training to 12 qubits, 1024 shots suffice for both; 10,000 halve the steps.
slide7_notes: Question one, the shot budget, treated as a hyperparameter. For each cost I computed how many shots per circuit are needed before the gradient signal is larger than the measurement noise. The local cost needs only 11 to 29 shots, even at 14 qubits. The global cost needs about 3.5 times more for every 2 extra qubits: 790 at 12 qubits and 3,740 at 14, far fewer than the usual worst-case estimate, because the noise of estimating a tiny probability is tiny too. Then I trained the teacher task at 256, 1024, 5000 and 10,000 shots. Up to 12 qubits, 1024 shots are already enough for both costs; more shots mostly make training faster: at 12 qubits the global cost needs a median of 271 steps with 1024 shots and 105 with 10,000 (local: 267 and 171). That matches the prediction: 1024 shots only run out for the global cost between 12 and 14 qubits. The 12-qubit point uses 5 seeds per setting, so treat its success rates as indicative. (~1.5 min)
